title: Frontend buries the animals' permanent address inside the identification form; Design release 1 asks for it as its own step in the consignment parties section

finding.frontend: The frontend has no permanent address page. For a commodity that needs one, the nine address fields are printed inside the animal identification card, between the identifier fields and the "Save and add another" button, under a small heading (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk:43-69). A trader meets the question only while entering identifiers for that animal, and the only route back to it is to reopen animal identification. On the captured page it appears once, on the dog line, and a trader scrolling for it has to know it is there.
finding.prototype: Design release 1 gives the question a page of its own, captioned "Consignment parties" and headed "Permanent address", reached from the parties list and back-linked to it (app/routes.js:2770-2777). It is a member of the consignment address sections for commodity code 01061900 alongside place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination (app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:124-131), so it is one step among the addresses a notification carries, answered once for every animal on that line and revisitable like any other.
finding.difference: Move the permanent address out of the identification card and give it its own page in the addresses section, listing every animal that needs one, so a trader can answer it, leave it and come back. The frontend already renders five party pages from one template driven by src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/parties.js, which is the shape this page takes; the obligation is already per-animal (permanentAddress sits within the unit record at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:200-208), so no model change is needed. Land this before the same-as-destination choice and the guidance copy, because both of those belong on the page this creates.
finding.falsifiedBy: A route, template or flow entry in the frontend that renders the animals' permanent address anywhere other than inside the identification card. src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk:43 is the only place the block is emitted, and the only frontend captures whose DOM contains the string "Permanent address" are the four states of the animal identification page — fe-animal-identification, fe-animal-identification-saved, fe-animal-identification-error and fe-animal-identification-at-maximum.
finding.verification: Ran the falsifier: grep for "Permanent address" across every file in capture/html/frontend returns exactly the four animal identification states named, and nothing else — not the hub, not the addresses list, not check your answers. Followed the Design release 1 route rather than taking the page on trust: the parties list renders "Add a permanent address" to /permanent-address (capture/html/prototype/dr1-roles-and-addresses-permanent-address.html:341-343), that route redirects to /permanent-address/select (app/routes.js:10789-10801), and /permanent-address/select renders the permanent-address-animals view with backLink /roles-and-addresses (app/routes.js:10821-10829 and :2770-2777). Confirmed the section is gated on commodity code at app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:124-131 and that the frontend obligation is per-unit-record at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:200-208. Read the identification card template whole and confirmed :43-69 is the only emission. Opened both page shots. CORRECT.
finding.correction: The claim stands, including the two structural legs a flow finding most often gets wrong — that Design release 1 reaches this from the parties list, and that Frontend's model already holds the address per animal. One detail for whoever builds it: the parties list links to /permanent-address, which clears any previous answer and redirects to /permanent-address/select before the page renders (app/routes.js:10789-10801), so the URL a user lands on is not the one the link names. Nothing else in either application renders this block.
